study type: Mechanistic animal study with a human observational sample collection component
exposure: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from NEC patients
outcome: Gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA gene sequencing)
cohort: Fecal samples were collected from 81 human neonates with Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC) and 81 matched controls (matched by gestational age, birth weight, date of birth, mode of delivery, and feeding patterns) which were then used for transplantation into germ-free mice.
finding: Colonization of germ-free mice with fecal microbiota from NEC patients, followed by a NEC-induction protocol, resulted in higher histological injury scores compared to mice colonized with control microbiota, driven by alterations in butyrate levels and a reduced T(reg)/CD4(+)T cell ratio.
cross-section timing: Fecal samples were collected from human neonates at the time of NEC diagnosis or from matched controls during the neonatal period.
birth_weight: Included in the study as a matching criterion for the human neonates whose fecal samples were used.
gest_age: Included in the study as a matching criterion for the human neonates whose fecal samples were used.
